edition: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026, version 1.3, May 2026

commodities.label: Gold
commodities.note: Gold content. Reserves are economically recoverable deposits, not central-bank holdings. Australia uses the broad national reserve estimate; its narrower JORC-compliant figure is 4,500 tonnes.

commodities.label: Silver
commodities.note: Silver content, including silver recovered as a byproduct. Australia uses the national reserve convention described in the source.

commodities.label: Copper
commodities.note: Copper content. Refinery output and mine output measure different stages; refined output can use imported material.

commodities.label: Lithium
commodities.note: Lithium content, not lithium carbonate equivalent. US mine output is withheld and the production world total excludes the United States.

commodities.label: Nickel
commodities.note: Nickel content. New Caledonia is separately reported by USGS and is outside this site’s 195-country scope; its output is not assigned to France.

commodities.label: Cobalt
commodities.note: Cobalt content. Reserve reporting conventions differ between national sources; refer to the source footnotes.

commodities.label: Bauxite
commodities.note: Dry bauxite ore, not aluminium metal. Bauxite and alumina are separate stages of the aluminium supply chain.

commodities.label: Alumina
commodities.note: Alumina production. This is aluminium oxide from refining, not primary aluminium metal.

commodities.label: Aluminium
commodities.note: Primary aluminium metal. Smelting location is not necessarily the location where the bauxite was mined.

commodities.label: Iron ore
commodities.note: Usable ore, contained iron and crude ore reserves are different measures. Production is reported in thousands of tonnes; reserves in millions. All values here are converted to tonnes.

commodities.label: Platinum
commodities.note: Platinum content. Source kilograms are converted to tonnes. The source publishes combined platinum-group reserves, not a separate platinum reserve ranking.

commodities.label: Palladium
commodities.note: Palladium content. Source kilograms are converted to tonnes. Combined platinum-group reserves cannot be treated as palladium alone.

commodities.label: Platinum-group metals
commodities.note: Combined platinum-group-metal content, including platinum, palladium and other PGMs. Source kilograms are converted to tonnes; this is not platinum-only or palladium-only reserves.

commodities.label: Rare earths
commodities.note: Rare-earth-oxide equivalent. Uses the revised May 2026 report: Brazil reserves are 11 million tonnes and Malaysia 710,000 tonnes. Greenland is outside this site’s country scope.

commodities.label: Diamonds (natural industrial)
commodities.note: Natural industrial diamonds only: excludes synthetic diamonds and gem-quality diamond production. Source million carats are converted to carats.

commodities.label: Graphite (natural)
commodities.note: Natural graphite only; synthetic graphite is excluded.

commodities.label: Lead
commodities.note: Lead content, not ore weight.

commodities.label: Zinc
commodities.note: Zinc content, not ore weight.

commodities.label: Tin
commodities.note: Tin content. Unknown reserves are omitted from rankings, not treated as zero.

commodities.label: Tungsten
commodities.note: Tungsten content. Withheld and unavailable values are not ranked.

commodities.label: Molybdenum
commodities.note: Molybdenum content, not concentrate weight. Production is reported in tonnes; reserves in thousands of tonnes. Both are converted to tonnes here.
